source: PROGRAM/FLAWS.md 0.1.0, FLAW-0013 example (a correct five-step proof that √2 is irrational, preceded by restated definitions of rational number, gcd and parity and three separate derivations of 2 | p² ⇒ 2 | p) and FLAW-0011 example (the same statement): executor-authored synthetic material, outside the S1 corpus (ADR-0011 D6)
title: The square root of two is irrational
statement: For all natural numbers $p$ and $q$ with $\gcd(p, q) = 1$, $p^2 \ne 2q^2$: the square root of two is irrational.

steps.text: Suppose, for contradiction, that $p^2 = 2q^2$ for natural numbers $p$ and $q$ with $\gcd(p, q) = 1$.
Then $p^2 = 2q^2$ is even, being twice the natural number $q^2$.
Hence $p$ is even: if $p$ were odd, $p^2$ would be odd, because the square of an odd number is odd. Write $p = 2k$.
fragment: rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one p with hp | hp
· have h1 : p ^ 2 % 2 = 1 := by rw [Nat.pow_mod, hp]

steps.text: Substituting, $4k^2 = 2q^2$, so $q^2 = 2k^2$ is even, and by the same argument $q$ is even. Write $q = 2m$.
fragment: have h4 : 2 * q ^ 2 = 2 * (2 * k ^ 2) := by rw [← hpq, hk]; ring
rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one q with hq | hq
· have h1 : q ^ 2 % 2 = 1 := by rw [Nat.pow_mod, hq]

steps.text: Thus $2$ divides both $p$ and $q$, so $2$ divides $\gcd(p, q) = 1$, which is absurd. Hence no such $p$ and $q$ exist, and $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.
fragment: have h2 : 2 ∣ Nat.gcd p q := Nat.dvd_gcd ⟨k, hk⟩ ⟨m, hm⟩

padding.text: Recall the definition of divisibility: for natural numbers $a$ and $b$, $a \mid b$ means that $b = ac$ for some natural number $c$; in particular $2 \mid b$ means $b = 2c$ for some $c$, and such a $b$ is called even.
padding.name: syndeom_s2_template_sqrt2_irrational_pad_dvd
padding.claim: ∀ a b : ℕ, a ∣ b ↔ ∃ c, b = a * c

padding.text: Recall that a rational number is a quotient $p/q$ of integers with $q \ne 0$, that every positive rational number has a representation in lowest terms with $p$ and $q$ natural numbers, and that $\gcd(p, q)$, the greatest common divisor, is the largest natural number dividing both $p$ and $q$; in particular it divides both.
padding.name: syndeom_s2_template_sqrt2_irrational_pad_gcd
padding.claim: ∀ p q : ℕ, Nat.gcd p q ∣ p ∧ Nat.gcd p q ∣ q
fragment: exact ⟨Nat.gcd_dvd_left p q, Nat.gcd_dvd_right p q⟩

padding.text: Recall that $p$ and $q$ are coprime when $\gcd(p, q) = 1$, which is exactly the condition that the fraction $p/q$ is in lowest terms.
padding.name: syndeom_s2_template_sqrt2_irrational_pad_coprime
padding.claim: ∀ p q : ℕ, Nat.Coprime p q ↔ Nat.gcd p q = 1

padding.text: Recall the definition of parity: a natural number $n$ is even when $2 \mid n$, that is, when $n \bmod 2 = 0$, and odd otherwise, that is, when $n \bmod 2 = 1$; every natural number is one or the other.
padding.name: syndeom_s2_template_sqrt2_irrational_pad_parity

padding.text: We check once more that if $2 \mid p^2$ then $2 \mid p$: the residue of $p^2$ modulo $2$ is the residue of $(p \bmod 2)^2$, so if $p \bmod 2 = 1$ then $p^2 \bmod 2 = 1$ and $2 \nmid p^2$; hence $p \bmod 2 = 0$.
padding.name: syndeom_s2_template_sqrt2_irrational_pad_two_dvd_sq_1
fragment: rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one p with hp | hp
· have h1 : p ^ 2 % 2 = 1 := by rw [Nat.pow_mod, hp]

padding.text: Here is a second derivation of the same fact: if $p$ were odd, say $p = 2m + 1$, then $p^2 = 4m^2 + 4m + 1 = 2(2m^2 + 2m) + 1$ would be odd, so $2 \nmid p^2$; therefore $2 \mid p^2$ forces $p$ to be even.
padding.name: syndeom_s2_template_sqrt2_irrational_pad_two_dvd_sq_2
fragment: rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one p with hp | hp
· obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ : ∃ m, p = 2 * m + 1 := ⟨p / 2, by omega⟩

padding.text: A third derivation: writing $p^2 = p \cdot p$, the residue of a product modulo $2$ is the product of the residues, so if $p \bmod 2 = 1$ then $p \cdot p \bmod 2 = 1 \cdot 1 = 1$, which is impossible when $2 \mid p^2$; hence $p$ is even.
padding.name: syndeom_s2_template_sqrt2_irrational_pad_two_dvd_sq_3
fragment: rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one p with hp | hp
· have h1 : p * p % 2 = 1 := by rw [Nat.mul_mod, hp]
